_comment: `entry-a` default-imports the external through a shim tree-shaking drops, so only `entry-a` observes it as an ES module. `entry-b` merely re-exports a *named* binding, and its sole live reference lives in `referenced_symbols_by_entry_point_chunk` rather than any included statement — the one path that never reaches the inclusion pass's statement walk. It must not wrap, since observer attribution is what keeps a named-only chunk off `__toESM` (see `chunk_recorded_external_interop`). Written originally to pin the panic that a wrapping `entry-b` hit with no runtime edge; observer attribution now stops it wrapping at all, so this pins the attribution instead and the panic path is only reachable if `patch_module_dependencies` is ever narrowed off bundle-wide. The bindings-less `require` of the runtime chunk in `entry-b` is that bundle-wide edge showing through — dead weight, not incorrect.
